item.title: China to Step Up Curbs Against Malicious Price Competition
item.description: China will step up scrutiny of malicious price competition, including cost investigations and price inspections of companies that engage in such practices, the State Administration for Market Regulation said at a State Council Information Office briefing on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China August Power Use Tops 1 Trillion kWh, Load Hits Record
item.description: China’s electricity consumption exceeded 1 trillion kilowatt-hours in August as power demand remained robust, the National Energy Administration said on its WeChat account Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China’s Smart-Glasses Sales Double in First Eight Months of Year
item.description: China’s sales of smart glasses on key platforms more than doubled in the first eight months of the year, while those of electrocardiogram monitors rose 75% and action cameras gained about 27%, the Ministry of Commerce said in a statement on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Australia’s Albanese Urges World to Act for Humanity in AI Race
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said middle powers have an important role to play in mitigating the risks posed by artificial intelligence and called for cooperation between the US and China.
item.dc:creator: Edward Johnson

item.title: Trump to Name AI Czar While Rejecting Safety Risks as a Hoax
item.description: President Donald Trump said he would name an artificial intelligence czar as he continued to push tech companies to race ahead with development despite growing fears safety.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: India’s Silicon Valley Is Straining Under Its Own Growth
item.description: Bangalore helped turn India into a global hub for software services, tech talent and outsourcing, building an ecosystem that now supports multinational firms, domestic startups and capital. But the city’s success has also become one of its biggest weaknesses. India still lacks the depth of capital available in the US and China, while Bangalore’s physical infrastructure has struggled to keep pace with private-sector growth. At the same time, southern India’s rising economic power is colliding with demographic and political shifts that could threaten its representation in the country’s Central Government, which helps support the growth that cities like Bangalore have enjoyed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: MBA Programs Race to Adapt to the AI Era
item.description: Stanford Graduate School of Business remains atop Bloomberg Businessweek’s US MBA rankings, scoring strongly in areas including compensation, networking and entrepreneurship. Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Editor Dimitra Kessenides is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that business schools are also experimenting with AI in teaching, case studies and career preparation as they try to ensure graduates have the skills employers increasingly expect. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CORRECT: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Takes a Long Bet
item.description:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon.
In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity.
